text:
ConocoPhillips shot up 3.55% today as oil prices spiked to a six-month high on escalating Middle East tensions. Brent crude jumped above $116 per barrel after the U.S. pulled diplomats from Saudi Arabia and signaled plans for strikes on Iran, with President Trump accusing Iran of manipulating oil markets. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly boost profits from both production and refining operations.

This move is part of a much larger two-week rally—the stock up 12.45% since mid-October—as geopolitical risks have fundamentally reshaped energy markets. The Iran situation is widening the gap between global oil ($115.22) and U.S. oil ($107.89), and reports show U.S. energy companies, particularly natural gas exporters, are benefiting as buyers shift away from unstable suppliers. For a diversified energy company with global operations, this regional conflict has become a tailwind rather than just headline noise.
